name: Title Fight
label: Revelation
lede: Two twelve-year-old twins and their friend took a name off a cable TV guide, built a stage in an abandoned pizza shop, and ended up pointing hardcore kids toward Dinosaur Jr. and shoegaze.

eras.title: Kingston, Pennsylvania, age twelve
eras.text: Ned and Ben Russin were twelve when they started Title Fight with Jamie Rhoden. Their older brother Alex Russin of Cold World had handed them punk records and a way into the hardcore circuit, and the kids took it from there, all the way to an abandoned pizza shop.

years.h: A cable guide gives Title Fight its name
years.p: Twins Ned (bass) and Ben Russin (drums), twelve years old, start the band in Kingston, Pennsylvania, with Jamie Rhoden on guitar. Ned finds the name on an old HBO/Showtime guide in the attic.
years.xp:
Their brother Alex Russin had given the twins [[Blink-182|0743b15a-3c32-48c8-ad58-cb325350befa]] and [[Pennywise|5c210861-2ce2-4be3-9307-bbcfc361cc01]] records around 1997. When Alex left for college, they raided the CDs he left behind and started learning instruments with a band in mind.

The first demo, Down for the Count, came out the same year, self-released.

years.h: Their first show is Frost Bite's last
years.p: Title Fight open the final show by Alex Russin's band Frost Bite, with [[Blacklisted|00330ad2-6d94-4957-b3b0-7ca1ea6f6fd6]], Drug Test and Scraps and Heartattacks on the bill.
years.xp: An early booking came from promoter Bobb Mac, who said yes to the kids on one condition: because of their brother Alex, they had to cover [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]]. Eight years later Gorilla Biscuits' [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]] produced their first album.

years.big: "Oh we'll just put on shows in here."
years.h: Teenagers turn an empty pizza restaurant into a venue
years.p: Ned Russin on the plan for The Future, summer 2005. The band built a stage, and the squat hosted [[Coalesce|3d722ad8-1986-4ce0-bc98-d0864ef625f2]], Mental, Renee Heartfelt and More to Pride before it shut.

years.h: Shane Moran makes it two guitars
years.p: The lineup settles, and the band starts drawing real attention in a Kingston, Scranton and Doylestown scene that includes [[Tigers Jaw|3cdf1327-39eb-4ffe-9ce3-20599ac6a468]] and [[Balance and Composure|0d20c42d-133c-429d-8f76-3c2458aee3e8]].

years.h: Jeff Casazza hears them on a Fireworks tour
years.p: The owner of Boston's Run for Cover Records catches the band on a summer run with [[Fireworks|7a7b70f3-1d6f-40f1-8c55-f75a376bee87]] and [[Set Your Goals|03d8f83e-a647-4bde-968a-189c0f147783]]. They also split a record with The Erection Kids on Flight Plan.

eras.title: Out of school, into the van
eras.text: The Kingston 7" pointed the band toward emo and melodic hardcore, and Run for Cover gave them a label. After The Last Thing You Forget all four members left school to tour full time, and their hometown lost its all-ages room.

years.h: The Kingston 7" leaves pop-punk behind
years.p: Flight Plan Records puts out the record that points Title Fight toward emo and melodic hardcore. In 2023 the band starts its own label, Purple Circle, to press it again.

years.h: Boston's Run for Cover Records signs Title Fight
years.p: By December they're at the Getaway Group in Massachusetts, recording with producer [[Jay Maas|8784da50-4dd3-4b54-8b01-948157c56f20]].

years.h: Four members drop out of school after The Last Thing You Forget
years.p: Three new Jay Maas-produced songs, with the CD gathering everything the band had released before. Artwork by John Slaby of Wilkes-Barre.
years.xp:
After it came out, all four members dropped out of school to tour full time, with [[Crime in Stereo|2bad20e7-61c8-4aa1-afcc-ca6f060ccb71]], Fireworks, [[New Found Glory|6acb932e-840d-47ac-8e0d-725ad8a6e52c]], [[Bayside|5f821136-9935-403c-abb5-e78ddda35e9f]], [[Senses Fail|b4946461-dacb-4aa9-a77c-7b3231317794]], Balance and Composure and [[H2O|b4307812-8143-46e0-9075-ffc06b30f3fe]].

Shane Moran and Jamie Rhoden also ran a hardcore side band, Bad Seed, whose 2009 EP came out on 6131 Records, while Moran and the Russins played in the straight edge band [[Disengage|cc0877e2-6c3c-4af6-904f-d5c1c6fc1fc4]].

years.cap: Title Fight playing to a packed room
years.h: The room where Title Fight played first shuts down
years.p: Cafe Metropolis closes in September, and the scene loses its all-ages home. The band's song Dreamcatchers lands on Triple B Records' America's Hardcore comp the same year.

eras.title: A Gilman-style room and a fuzz record
eras.text: Gorilla Biscuits' Walter Schreifels produced the debut album, the band opened its own all-ages space modeled on 924 Gilman, and Floral Green sent hardcore kids to Dinosaur Jr. and Sonic Youth. It reached the Billboard 200.

years.h: SideOneDummy signs them for a first full-length
years.p: The free single 27 follows on February 10, a few months ahead of the debut.

years.h: Title Fight open an all-ages room of their own
years.p: Title Fight and local friends run the Redwood Art Space as all-ages and alcohol-free, modeled on Berkeley's 924 Gilman Street. Landlord and government pressure force a move in June 2012.

years.h: A Gorilla Biscuits veteran produces Shed
years.p: [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]] of Gorilla Biscuits and [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]] produces the debut, [[Will Yip|282e2957-fd09-4260-babf-50f1d57eeb75]] engineers, and Schreifels sings on Safe in Your Skin. It debuts at No. 8 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.
years.xp:
The kids who'd been made to cover Gorilla Biscuits at an early show now had Schreifels producing. Will Yip engineered and mixed. The album runs 27 minutes and 17 seconds.

Critics were warm: Metacritic lands at 81, and NME, Rock Sound and AbsolutePunk each gave it 8/10.

years.cap: Title Fight at The Peel, Kingston upon Thames, England, December 2011
years.h: England's Reading and Leeds festivals book Title Fight
years.p: They arrive after a first headline tour with [[The Menzingers|3071d829-b9ca-4499-b4f5-74d6d8531aed]] and [[Touché Amoré|ea367e3c-4c74-460b-8a99-bbbb9b1ad5cf]] and a July run through the UK and Europe.

years.cap: Title Fight on a festival stage, July 2012
years.h: Japan first, then the US with Rise Against
years.p: Title Fight play Japan's Alliance Trax A.T. Tour in February, then open for [[Rise Against|606bf117-494f-4864-891f-09d63ff6aa4b]] across the US in April and May.

years.h: Fuzz replaces pop-punk on Floral Green
years.p: Will Yip produces, with [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]], [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] and [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] in its DNA. It debuts at No. 69 on the Billboard 200; NPR premiered Sympathy in August.
years.xp:
BrooklynVegan's Andrew Sacher later called it one of the most pivotal albums of its generation, for hardcore and for guitar-based rock and punk in general, and credited it with helping set up hardcore's 2020s breakthrough.

The record release show was in Warrior Run, Pennsylvania, with The Menzingers, Tigers Jaw and Gypsy. The same month Title Fight made their first trip to Australia, with Touché Amoré.

eras.title: Four songs for Revelation, then a left turn
eras.text: Between Floral Green and Hyperview, Title Fight stopped at Revelation, the label behind the Gorilla Biscuits records they'd been made to cover as kids, for four songs. Then they signed to ANTI- and made a shoegaze album.

years.h: Touché Amoré takes the other side of a split 7"
years.p: The two bands had already toured the US and Australia together.

years.h: Spring Songs packs four songs into twelve minutes
years.p: Will Yip produces. Revelation's first pressing runs 1,512 on clear orange and 2,650 on opaque orange vinyl.
years.xp:
SPIN premiered Be a Toy in August. Its video, directed by Susy Cereijo, was shot on Super 8 during the band's spring European tour.

Revelation said the deal gave Title Fight room to move, and the band used it. Pitchfork gave the EP 7.2; Vice didn't like it.

years.cap: Title Fight at Carioca Club, Sao Paulo, January 2014
years.h: From a pizza-shop squat to Coachella
years.p: Less than a decade after building a stage in an empty pizza restaurant, Title Fight play Coachella.

years.h: ANTI- signs Title Fight, and Studio 4 fills the summer
years.p: They spend July and August in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania, making Hyperview with Will Yip.

years.h: Character actor Mark Burnham stars in the Chlorine video
years.p: The Fader premieres the clip, directed by Johnny Look. Pitchfork hears No Age and DIIV in its flanged guitars, not Warped Tour.

years.h: Hyperview trades fuzz for jangle
years.p: A shoegaze and dream pop record, with Ned Russin citing [[The Beach Boys|ebfc1398-8d96-47e3-82c3-f782abcdb13d]]' Pet Sounds. It reaches No. 78 on the Billboard 200; the release show is at the Gallery of Sound record store in Wilkes-Barre.
years.xp:
The band defined the title as "a state of increased vision, of acute awareness. One in which foresight is even sharper than hindsight." Ned Russin called it the most melodic, simple stuff they'd ever written.

Exclaim!'s Branan Ranjanathan wrote that the fuzzy wall of sound from before had been replaced by lead guitar jangle. Metacritic landed at 71.

The tours that year paired them with Merchandise and [[Power Trip|7f179acc-d6eb-4ca9-af90-c14e397fb613]] in the US, and with Milk Teeth, Cold World and [[Drug Church|32d2897c-4c91-46db-8161-f51d3f4f0d93]] in Europe.

eras.title: No announcement
eras.text: Title Fight never announced a breakup. They played less, then a festival in England, then a benefit on Long Island, and then nothing, while each of them started something else.

years.h: An unreleased song goes to Orlando
years.p: After the Pulse nightclub shooting, the Hyperview outtake Dust Collector goes onto Forever Beautiful, a Bandcamp comp for the OneOrlando Fund with Turnstile, Citizen and Modern Baseball.

years.big: "If this is it, it's been a wild and beautiful ride."
q: If this is it, it's been a wild and beautiful ride.
years.h: Headlining Outbreak, Ned Russin hints at the end
years.p: At England's Outbreak Festival, their second-to-last show, he tells the crowd this might be it. The same year he starts his solo project [[Glitterer|fb29a165-203d-497b-9a01-fc48f4dba65c]].

years.h: Title Fight's last show goes to a friend's family
years.p: A benefit at Revolution Bar & Music Hall in Amityville, New York, for longtime friend and tour mate Aaron Warman and his family. [[Turnstile|7b748dac-f5ce-45a7-9b95-c1d8b5b013ed]], King Nine and Nosebleed share the bill.
years.xp: The band's announcement said it plainly: "We are playing a show in support of our long time friend/tour mate Aaron Warman and his family."

eras.title: A B-side takes over TikTok
eras.text: With the band silent, a Shed deep cut became their biggest song, the hardcore boom they'd helped set up arrived, and Ben Russin joined Citizen. Ned Russin kept saying the same thing: nobody ever said it was over.

years.big: "Title Fight was the first one that really affected everybody."
q: Title Fight was the first one that really affected everybody.
years.h: Safe in Your Skin goes viral, eleven years late
years.p: Citizen's Mat Kerekes on the band's reach. On TikTok in 2022 and 2023 the Shed track Walter Schreifels sings on takes off, and by November 2025 it's their most-streamed Spotify song at 118 million plays, though it was never a single.
years.xp: Wikipedia's list of bands citing Title Fight runs from Turnover and The Story So Far to Ethel Cain.

years.h: Ben Russin takes the drum stool in Citizen
years.p: He plays on their album Calling the Dogs. In September, members of Title Fight start the Purple Circle label to re-press Kingston.

years.h: Title Fight play together again, at a wedding
years.p: Ned Russin, Jamie Rhoden and Shane Moran play acoustic at drummer Ben Russin's wedding, their first time together since 2018, covering Walter Schreifels's Requiem. Alex Russin joins Rhoden on [[Oasis|39ab1aed-75e0-4140-bd47-540276886b60]]'s Slide Away.
years.xp:
Stereogum compared it to stories of Fugazi quietly practicing in D.C. basements: a reunion for themselves and nobody else.

Ned Russin's line on the band's status hasn't changed: they never said hiatus, never said broken up, and any band might play again.
